articles.title: Law And Procedure For Pre-Deposit For Tribunal Appeals In GST
articles.summary: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) law has been amended under Section 112(8) to reduce the pre-deposit required for filing tribunal appeals to 10% of the disputed amount. The amendment also revises the maximum deposit limits and specifies that a 10% deposit applies even for penalty-only demands. This change aims to ease the financial burden on taxpayers appealing against GST orders in tribunals.
articles.raw_summary: GST Section 112(8) reduces Tribunal appeal pre-deposit to 10%, with revised maximum limits and 10% deposit for penalty-only demands. The post Law And Procedure For Pre-Deposit For Tribunal Appeals In GST appeared first on TaxGuru .

articles.title: Teacher's Writ Petition Against Private School Maintainable To Enforce Statutory Pay Scale : Supreme Court
articles.summary: The Supreme Court ruled that a writ petition filed by a teacher against a private school to enforce statutory pay scales is maintainable, as rights derived from a statute can be enforced if they have a public element. The Court emphasized that statutory duties with public significance can be enforced through judicial intervention. This ruling impacts private school teachers' pay scales and could influence labor policies for private educational institutions.
articles.raw_summary: When the rights flow from a statute, a writ petition is maintainable to enforce them if the duty has a public element, the Court stated.

articles.summary: Parliament has approved the MMDR Amendment Bill 2026, which empowers the central government to set conditions on state-imposed taxes, cess, and other levies related to mining rights and mineral-bearing lands. The bill reflects a shift in regulatory authority over the mining sector.

U.S. crude and distillate inventories declined, while gasoline stocks increased.

US crude and distillate inventories fell last week while gasoline stocks rose.

articles.title: Ashok Leyland just had a record June quarter. So why did the margin fall a full point?
articles.summary: Ashok Leyland's June-quarter has an unusual contradiction. The company sold 48,763 commercial vehicles, its highest-ever first-quarter volume, and revenue from operations rose 10.43% to Rs. 9,634 crore. Yet, the operating EBITDA was Rs. 970 crore, almost the same as a year earlier. The Q1 FY 27 result must, therefore, be understood not in terms of greater demand, but in terms of why the record volumes and revenue did not lead to an increase in operating earnings.
